problem: math-p0039: does every finite flag-transitive projective plane have to be Desarguesian?
premises: Kantor 1987 (uses CFSG): a non-Desarguesian flag-transitive plane has n even, p = n^2+n+1 prime, sharply flag-transitive Frobenius group
Thas-Zagier 2008 Prop. 2.1/Thm. 2.4/Sec. 2: the plane is the development of D = mu_(n+1) in F_p; PG(2,2) and PG(2,8) are the only special planes that are Desarguesian
Feit 1990 valid conditions: 8 | n (Lemma 2.2; parent also cites Jungnickel-Vedder) and d^(n+1) = 1 (mod p) for divisors d of n, giving n = 8 (mod 24)

exact_conditional_exclusion.statement: Under the premises, no non-Desarguesian flag-transitive projective plane has order n < 2582236504064.

structural.theorem: For a >= 3 and P = 4^a+2^a+1 (prime or not), {2^i mod P : 0 <= i < 3a} is a Sidon set (fails at a = 2).
structural.corollary: For n = 2^a with p prime, the forced subgroup <2> (2, all divisors of n, mu_3) admits no repeated nonzero difference, so such certificates cannot exclude n; further exclusions need additional information whose form the theorem does not prescribe.
structural.remark: Singer's planar set of PG(2,2^a) contains <2> (checked a = 3, 9; general a via Cohen's trace theorem, abstract/introduction read only).
structural.minor_lemma: u-1 not in +-D for u in D minus {1,2,1/2}; in particular -3 not in D. Does not exclude n = 512.

power_two_family.excluded: every n = 2^a with 3 < a < 177147 (with attack-e2 t = 2..9)
